    segmantR: Cell Segmentation for Histology with Human-in-the-Loop Training

    Source: R/segmantR-package.R
    segmantR-package.Rd

    Cell segmentation for histology and multiplexed tissue imaging: classical methods that run in R alone, optional deep learning backends through 'reticulate', a human-in-the-loop correction and training workflow, and reproducible exchange with 'QuPath' and partner packages.

    Where to start

    • Images and masks: new_sg_image(), sg_read_image(), new_sg_mask(), and the synthetic examples from sg_example_image() and sg_example_mask().

    • Segmentation: sg_segment_threshold(), sg_segment_watershed() and sg_segment_propagate() need no Python; sg_segment_cellpose(), sg_segment_stardist() and sg_segment_mesmer() use a Python environment selected with sg_setup_python().

    • Measurement and evaluation: sg_extract_features(), sg_evaluate_segmentation().

    • Figures: sg_plot_overlay(), sg_plot_mask(), sg_plot_features(), sg_plot_comparison(), sg_plot_metrics().

    • Reproducible runs and exchange: sg_protocol_run(), sg_export_interchange(), sg_import_interchange(), sg_export_qupath().

    • Interactive correction: sg_app() and sg_run_app().

    See vignette("segmantR") for a first workflow and vignette("protocols-and-interop") for protocols and exchange formats.
